mainTopic: עירובין 43a: whether רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע argue about a moving boat or only a stopped one, and רב חנניא's question whether תחומין apply above ten טפחים
overview: This amud finishes רבי זירא's explanation of the boat dispute in the משנה: for רבי יהושע, a boat's walls are only there to keep water out, so they are not real מחיצות. רבה explains the dispute differently. In a moving boat everyone agrees a person may walk the whole boat, and the argument is only about a boat that has stopped. רב נחמן בר יצחק proves this from the משנה's word רָצוּ: רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא 'wanted' to be strict, so their strictness was voluntary. רב אשי adds that the משנה groups the boat with a fixed pen and stable. רב אחא בריה דרבא objects that a ruling of הלכה about a boat shows there was a real dispute. רב אשי agrees that there was a dispute, about the stopped boat, and brings a ברייתא in which רבי יהושע himself decided the הלכה. Then רב חנניא asks a new question: do תחומין apply more than ten טפחים above the ground, for example on a narrow post, in a leap, or on a boat? The גמרא tries to answer it from the boat stories in the משנה, from seven teachings heard in סורא and פומבדיתא on the same שבת, and finally from a ברייתא about a vow of נזירות on the day משיח comes. That last proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Boat walls are only meant to keep the water out
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of רבי זירא's explanation: according to רבי יהושע, a boat's walls exist to keep out water, not to make a living space.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The boat's walls] are made to keep water out.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of רבי זירא's explanation. He is giving the reason why, according to רבי יהושע, the walls of a boat do not count as walls for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walls normally turn an area into one 'space' for שבת, so a person could walk all of it. רבי זירא says רבי יהושע does not treat a boat's walls this way. Their purpose is to keep the sea out, not to create a place to live. Therefore they do not count as true מחיצות.

keyTerms.meaning: are made / designed (refers to the walls)
partitions / walls that define a space for שבת

phrases.english: they are made to keep the water out.
phrases.notes: The subject is the walls of the boat. These are the closing words of רבי זירא's reasoning for רבי יהושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי זירא's explanation, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע, a boat's walls are not living-space partitions, because their purpose is only to keep water out.

steps.title: Why did רבה not explain it like רבי זירא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבה chose a different explanation of the dispute instead of following רבי זירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה: what is his reason that he did not say like רבי זירא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבה did not accept רבי זירא's explanation of the dispute. This question sets up the next step, where רבה's reason is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's partition explanation sounds reasonable, so the גמרא wants to know what pushed רבה away from it. The answer will show that רבה reads the scope of the dispute differently.

phrases.english: And Rabba, what is the reason
phrases.notes: רבה already gave his own explanation earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: that he did not say like Rabbi Zeira?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבה's view with the רבי זירא explanation that just ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What made רבה reject רבי זירא's explanation of the dispute?

steps.title: In a moving boat everyone agrees; the dispute is only about a stopped boat
steps.stepSummary: רבה holds that the תנאים do not argue about a moving boat at all. They argue only about a boat that has stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the boat is moving, everyone agrees [one may walk the whole boat]. When do they disagree? When it has stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבה. In a moving boat no one argues, and the whole disagreement is about a boat that is standing still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה limits the dispute to a stationary boat. In a moving boat, even רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא agree that walking the entire boat is permitted. This is why רבה could not explain the dispute the way רבי זירא did.

keyTerms.meaning: when it has stopped / is stationary

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה: moving boat means everyone permits walking the whole boat. Stationary boat is where רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע disagree.

phrases.english: Regarding a moving boat, everyone agrees.
phrases.notes: Even רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא allow walking the whole boat.

phrases.english: When they disagree is when it has stopped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה holds that the dispute does not apply to a moving boat at all, only to a stationary one.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the משנה's wording supports this
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the משנה itself shows that there is no dispute about a moving boat. He then quotes the story from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Our משנה also implies that they do not disagree about a moving boat. From where? From what it teaches: It happened that they came from פלנדרסין and their boat sailed out to sea. רבן גמליאל and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה walked the whole boat, but רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא did not move beyond four אמות, because they wanted to be strict on themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק announces that the משנה's wording supports רבה's view. He quotes the story the proof will rest on, which sets up the actual proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story describes a boat that had sailed out, so it was moving. In it, two Sages walked the whole boat and two stayed within four אמות. The key word to watch is רָצוּ, 'they wanted', which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה is also precise (it implies this too)
from where? (how do we see it?)
four cubits (the basic personal space on שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the משנה shows that רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא held walking was forbidden. The proof depends on the word רָצוּ, 'they wanted', which hints that their strictness was voluntary.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Our Mishnah is also precise [in implying]
that regarding a moving boat they do not disagree.
From where? From that which it teaches:
An incident where they were coming from Pelandarsin
and their boat sailed out to sea.
phrases.notes: The boat was moving. This detail is key to the proof.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
walked the entire boat,
while Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Akiva
did not move beyond four cubits,
because they wanted to be strict on themselves.
phrases.notes: The word רָצוּ ('they wanted') is the basis of the proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for רבה's position in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the תנאים do not disagree about a moving boat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story in the משנה about the boat that sailed from פלנדרסין, and its wording 'שרצו להחמיר על עצמן'.

steps.title: The word 'they wanted' shows the strictness was voluntary
steps.stepSummary: If there is no dispute about a moving boat, the word רָצוּ makes sense. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא were not required to be strict, but chose to be, in case the boat stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say they do not disagree about a moving boat. That is why it teaches 'they wanted': [they were strict] in case the boat would stop.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the proof. The word 'they wanted' only fits if the law did not require strictness on a moving boat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהושע held that walking a moving boat was truly forbidden, the משנה would not say they 'wanted' to be strict. It would simply describe the law. The word רָצוּ shows a voluntary extra stringency, worried that the boat might stop and enter the stationary case, where they hold walking is forbidden. This supports רבה: in a moving boat there is no real dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: it works well if you say

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's word רָצוּ shows that רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא were being voluntarily strict on a moving boat, out of concern it might stop. This supports רבה: everyone permits walking the whole boat when it is moving.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic case of a 'דיוק' from a single word in the משנה. The precise choice of a word reveals the legal status: optional strictness versus required law.

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that regarding a moving boat they do not disagree —
that is why it teaches 'they wanted',
[out of concern] that perhaps it will stop.
phrases.notes: Their strictness was a precaution in case the boat stopped, which is the case they do disagree about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא בִּמְהַלֶּכֶת לָא פְּלִיגִי הַיְינוּ דְּקָתָנֵי רָצוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That on a moving boat, walking the whole boat is permitted according to everyone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word רָצוּ in the משנה, which shows voluntary rather than required strictness.

steps.title: If they argued about a moving boat, 'they chose to be strict' would make no sense
steps.stepSummary: This finishes רב נחמן בר יצחק's proof. If רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא held that a moving boat is forbidden, being careful there would be required. It would not be a voluntary stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say they do argue about a moving boat, then this phrase 'they chose to be strict' is wrong, because by their view it is an outright prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the proof from Step 5 by showing the other side. If there were a dispute about a moving boat, the משנה's wording would not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story, רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא held back while the boat was moving, and the משנה says they 'chose to be strict' (רָצוּ לְהַחֲמִיר). If they held that walking around a moving boat is forbidden, the משנה would not call it a choice, because they would simply be keeping the law. So the wording shows they agreed that a moving boat is permitted.

phrases.english: But if you say they disagree (about a moving boat),
this phrase 'they chose to be strict' —
phrases.notes: Quoting the words of the משנה's story.

phrases.english: it is an actual prohibition!
phrases.notes: So it should not be called a voluntary choice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided proof begun in Step 5 by showing the opposite view does not fit the text.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's view that there is no dispute about a moving boat
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording 'רָצוּ לְהַחֲמִיר' in the משנה's story

steps.title: רב אשי: the boat is listed with a pen and a stable, so it means a stopped boat
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings a second proof from the משנה. Because the boat appears next to a pen and a stable, it must also be something fixed in place, meaning a boat that has stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is also precise this way. It teaches 'a boat' alongside 'a pen and a stable.' Just as a pen and a stable are fixed in place, so too the boat is one that is fixed in place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds another proof for רבה's approach. This proof comes from how the משנה groups its cases together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists three walled places together: a pen, a stable, and a boat. A pen and a stable never move. Grouping the boat with them suggests the משנה is talking about a boat that is standing still. That means the dispute is about a stopped boat, not a moving one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is precise (the wording proves the point)
A pen and a stable (enclosures for animals)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The Mishnah is also precise (on this point),
for it teaches: a boat,
parallel to a pen and a stable.
Just as a pen and a stable are fixed in place,
so too the boat is one that is fixed in place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent proof from the משנה for the same point.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's view that the dispute is only about a stopped boat
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה lists a boat together with a pen and a stable

steps.title: Challenge: a ruling of הלכה shows there was a real dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges רב אשי. There is a ruling that 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל regarding a boat.' Deciding the הלכה only makes sense if there was a real argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: 'The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל regarding a boat.' Saying 'the הלכה' proves that they disagreed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges the idea that the תנאים did not truly argue about the boat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only need to decide 'the הלכה follows X' when two sides really argue. The phrase 'they chose to be strict' made it sound like there was no real argument. So a ruling of הלכה on the boat seems to show that a real dispute did exist.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
'The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel regarding a boat' —
'the halacha' implies that they disagree!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of Steps 5-7 that there was no real argument about the boat.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'רָצוּ לְהַחֲמִיר' means there was no real dispute about the boat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling of הלכה is only issued where there is a genuine dispute, so the ruling shows the תנאים truly argued.

steps.title: Yes, they argue, about the stopped boat, and רבי יהושע decided the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי agrees that there is a real dispute, but it is about a boat that has stopped. A ברייתא from רבי יהושע's nephew confirms that they argued all day and that רבי יהושע decided the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, they do disagree. It was taught in a ברייתא: חנניא, the son of רבי יהושע's brother, says: 'That whole day they sat and discussed the הלכה. In the evening my father's brother decided: the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל regarding a boat, and the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא regarding a pen and a stable.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. He agrees that there is a real dispute, and he brings a ברייתא showing that a ruling was actually made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction. The 'chose to be strict' wording is about the moving boat, where nobody argued. The real dispute, which needed a ruling, is about the boat once it stopped, just as רבה said. The ברייתא shows that רבי יהושע himself settled the matter, ruling one way for a boat and the other way for a pen and a stable.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was taught in a ברייתא
My father's brother, my uncle (here, רבי יהושע)

steps.whatToRemember: There was no argument about a moving boat; even רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא held back there only by choice. The real argument, which was decided by רבי יהושע, concerns a boat at rest. There the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל, while for a pen and a stable it follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אִין' does not mean רב אשי gave up his proof. He agrees there is a dispute, but only about the stopped boat. The moving boat remains undisputed.

phrases.english: Yes (they disagree),
and it was taught in a baraita:
Chananya (the son of Rabbi Yehoshua's brother) says:
That whole day
they sat and discussed the matter of halacha;
in the evening my father's brother decided:
the halacha follows Rabban Gamliel regarding a boat,
and the halacha follows Rabbi Akiva regarding a pen and a stable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 by limiting the real dispute to the stopped boat and citing a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the dispute but limits its scope to the stopped boat
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ruling of הלכה seemed to contradict the claim that there was no real dispute.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute, and the ruling, concern the stopped boat. The moving boat remains undisputed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the practical הלכה: a boat follows רבן גמליאל, while a pen and a stable follow רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רב חנניא asks whether שבת boundaries apply above ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: רב חנניא asks whether the rule of תחומין applies to someone more than ten טפחים above the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנניא asked: Do the שבת boundaries (תחומין) apply more than ten טפחים above the ground, or do they not apply up there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. רב חנניא wants to know whether the שבת walking limit applies only on the ground, or also high in the air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a person may not walk beyond his תחום. רב חנניא asks whether this limit covers all space, or only the area within ten טפחים of the ground. If it covers only the area near the ground, then moving past the limit while more than ten טפחים up would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question that the גמרא wants to solve)
The שבת boundaries, the limit of how far one may walk
Higher than ten טפחים above the ground

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section depends on this question. The boat discussion before it and the cases after it both depend on whether the area above ten טפחים counts for תחומין.

phrases.english: Rav Chananya asked:
Do Shabbos boundaries apply above ten handbreadths,
or do Shabbos boundaries not apply above ten handbreadths?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question. It is linked in theme to the earlier boat discussion, because a boat is high above the riverbed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule of תחומין apply to the space more than ten טפחים above the ground?

steps.title: A wide post is not a question because it counts as ground
steps.stepSummary: A post that is ten טפחים high and four wide is not part of the question. It counts as solid ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the case is a post that is ten טפחים high and four טפחים wide, you should not be asking about it, because it is solid ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is narrowing the question. It removes a case that is not really in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A post that is 4×4 טפחים and ten high is a real, usable surface. So it counts as the ground itself, only raised up. Walking on it is like walking on the earth, so תחומין clearly apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: You should not ask about this; it is obvious

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not 'is a high place exempt?' A wide, solid surface counts as ground no matter how high it is. The question is only about being up in the air without a real surface.

phrases.english: A post ten handbreadths high and four wide,
you should not ask about it,
because it is solid ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רב חנניא's question by removing a case that is obvious.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A post ten טפחים high and four wide counts as ground, so תחומין apply on it.

steps.title: The real question: a narrow post, or a person leaping
steps.stepSummary: The question applies to a post that is ten high but less than four wide, or to a person moving through the air by leaping.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case you should ask about is a post that is ten טפחים high but not four טפחים wide. Or another case: a person who travels by leaping through the air above ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now names the exact cases where רב חנניא's question is real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A narrow post is not a usable surface, so it does not count as ground. A person on it, or a person flying through the air in a leap, is truly 'above ten' and not on the ground. So the question is real in both cases: does the תחום reach up there?

keyTerms.meaning: The case where you should ask
And it is not four טפחים wide
A leap or jump through the air

phrases.english: Where you should ask is
about a post ten handbreadths high
but not four handbreadths wide.
Alternatively, where he travels by leaping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out the wide post, it names the cases the question is really about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The question applies only where there is no usable surface: a narrow post, or a person moving through the air by leaping.

steps.title: Another version: the question is asked about a boat
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב חנניא's question is about a boat sailing more than ten טפחים above the riverbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: what is the law for a boat? Do תחומין apply to it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the question. In this version, the case is a boat on water, which is high above the bottom of the river or sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the space 'above ten' is the water under the boat. The water is deeper than ten טפחים below the person. So the question is whether someone in a boat has left the area where תחומין apply. This connects directly to the earlier discussion of רבן גמליאל and the boat.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חנניא asks whether תחומין apply higher than ten טפחים. The question is not about a wide post, which counts as ground. It is about a narrow post or a leap, or, in another version, a boat.

phrases.english: Another version:
Regarding a boat, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of רב חנניא's question, moving the case from a post or a leap to a boat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do תחומין apply to someone in a boat who is more than ten טפחים above the riverbed?

steps.title: Proof from the Sages who were strict on the boat
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא brings a proof from the משנה's story of the boat sailing from פלנדרסין. רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא were strict and stayed within four אמות. That only makes sense if תחומין apply even above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: Come and hear a proof. The משנה tells of the Sages coming from פלנדרסין when their boat sailed on the sea. If you say תחומין apply above ten טפחים, that is why רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא wanted to be strict. But if you say תחומין do not apply there, why did they want to be strict?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא tries to answer רב חנניא's question with a story from the משנה. He argues that it shows תחומין do apply above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא would not walk more than four אמות on the sailing boat because they wanted to be strict on themselves. Being strict only makes sense if there is a real possibility that תחומין apply. A boat sailing on the deep sea is far more than ten טפחים above the seabed, so the story seems to show that תחומין apply even up there.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the formula for bringing a proof from a source
שבת boundaries: the limit beyond which one may not walk
It makes sense (granted): introduces the side that fits the source
פלנדרסין, the place the Sages were sailing from
They wanted (to be strict on themselves)

steps.confusionAlert: The word רצו here does not mean 'they ran.' It refers back to the משנה's phrase 'רצו להחמיר על עצמן', 'they wanted to be strict on themselves.'

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said: Come and hear:
It once happened that they were coming from Pelandarsin
and their boat sailed out on the sea, etc.
It makes sense if you say there are boundaries (above ten handbreadths):
that is why they wanted (to be strict).
But if you say there are no boundaries (there),
why did they want (to be strict)?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רב חנניא's question about a boat sailing more than ten טפחים above the bottom.
steps.raayaObject: That תחומין apply above ten טפחים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the Sages sailing from פלנדרסין, where רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא were strict.

steps.title: The boat was in shallow swampy water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Following רבא's approach elsewhere, the boat was moving through shallow swampy water, within ten טפחים of the bottom, where תחומין certainly apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said, the case is a boat moving through shallow swampy water. Here too, the boat was moving through shallow swampy water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off רב הושעיא's proof. It says the boat in the story may not have been more than ten טפחים above the bottom at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the water was shallow, the boat was within ten טפחים of the seabed, so it counts like ground level. There, everyone agrees תחומין apply. The story therefore tells us nothing about the case above ten טפחים, so רב חנניא's question is still unresolved. The next step brings another proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: applies the same answer to this case

phrases.english: As Rava said:
(the case is) where it was moving through shallow swampy water;
here too, it was moving through shallow swampy water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 14 by explaining the משנה's case differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the strictness of רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the boat was more than ten טפחים above the bottom. It may have been in shallow water within ten טפחים.

steps.title: Proof from arriving at the port after dark
steps.stepSummary: A second proof from the משנה. When they reached port after dark, they asked רבן גמליאל whether they could get off, and he answered that they had been inside the תחום before nightfall. That answer only matters if תחומין apply above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: once they did not enter the port until after dark. If you say תחומין apply above ten טפחים, it makes sense that they asked. But if you say תחומין do not apply there, what difference would it make whether or not they had been inside the תחום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story from the same משנה to try again to prove that תחומין apply above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל permitted them to get off the boat because he had seen that they were already within the city's תחום before שבת began. If the boat was above ten טפחים and תחומין did not apply there, they would never have acquired a fixed שבת place out at sea. They could simply walk off, so being 'inside the תחום' would not matter. His reasoning therefore seems to show that תחומין do apply.

phrases.english: Come and hear: once

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִכְנְסוּ לַנָּמָל עַד שֶׁחָשֵׁיכָה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: they did not enter the port until it got dark, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא יֵשׁ תְּחוּמִין — שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: It makes sense if you say there are boundaries (above ten): that is fine.
But if you say there are no boundaries,
even if we had not been within the boundary,
what difference would it make!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פַּעַם אַחַת לֹא נִכְנְסוּ לַנָּמָל עַד שֶׁחָשֵׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new proof is brought from a different story in the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That תחומין apply above ten טפחים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה where רבן גמליאל permitted getting off because they had been inside the תחום before dark.

steps.title: רבא: again, shallow swampy water
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the second proof the same way. The boat was in shallow swampy water, within ten טפחים of the bottom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the case is a boat moving through shallow swampy water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes off the second proof with the same answer. The boat was close to the bottom, so this story does not prove anything about the case above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Within ten טפחים of the bottom, the boat counts like ground, so תחומין certainly apply and רבן גמליאל's reasoning makes sense. Since both stories can be explained this way, neither one settles רב חנניא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא, the אמורא who gives the shallow-water answer
Ten handbreadths: the height at issue in רב חנניא's question
The ground (here, the sea or river bottom)

steps.whatToRemember: Both boat stories in the משנה can be explained as cases of shallow water (רקק), within ten טפחים of the bottom. So neither one proves whether תחומין apply higher than ten טפחים. רב חנניא's question is still unresolved, and the גמרא tries other proofs in steps 18-20.

phrases.english: Rava said:
(It was) moving through shallow swampy water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 16 the same way step 15 rejected step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבן גמליאל's answer at the port.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the boat was more than ten טפחים above the bottom. It may have been in shallow water.

steps.title: Proof from the seven teachings carried from סורא to פומבדיתא on שבת
steps.stepSummary: Seven teachings were said on שבת morning before רב חסדא in סורא and that same afternoon before רבא in פומבדיתא. The גמרא suggests אליהו brought them by flying, so תחומין must not apply above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: there were seven teachings that were said on שבת morning before רב חסדא in סורא, and toward the end of that same שבת before רבא in פומבדיתא. Who said them? Wasn't it אליהו? So we see that תחומין do not apply above ten טפחים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof, this time from a real event, to show that תחומין do not apply above ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סורא and פומבדיתא are too far apart to walk between on שבת, yet the same teachings showed up in both places on the same day. The guess is that אליהו carried them by flying through the air. אליהו keeps שבת and would never break a law, so flying high above the ground must not count as leaving the תחום.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. The usual way the גמרא opens a proof.
A teaching or statement of הלכה
Toward evening, near the end of the day
אליהו הנביא, who keeps the מצוות and can travel miraculously
Apparently, so we see. It introduces the conclusion drawn from a proof.

steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not say that אליהו broke שבת. It works the other way: because אליהו certainly did NOT break שבת, his flying must have been allowed. That would mean there are no תחומין above ten טפחים.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
these seven teachings that were said
in the morning on Shabbat
before Rav Chisda in Sura,
toward evening on that Shabbat
before Rava in Pumbedita.
Who said them (brought them over)?
Was it not Eliyahu who said them?
phrases.notes: He traveled miraculously through the air

phrases.english: Apparently, there are no Shabbat limits above ten handbreadths!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both proofs from the boat משנה were rejected, the גמרא tries a new kind of proof: a story from the אמוראים.
steps.raayaObject: That תחומין do not apply above ten טפחים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The event of the seven teachings said in סורא and in פומבדיתא on the same שבת, which the גמרא assumes אליהו brought

steps.title: Maybe a demon who does not keep שבת brought the teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Perhaps יוסף שידא, a demon who does not keep שבת, carried the teachings, so nothing can be learned about תחומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Maybe יוסף שידא (Yosef the demon) said them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by offering a different messenger who does not keep שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended completely on the messenger being אליהו, someone who keeps the הלכה. If the messenger was יוסף שידא, who doesn't care about שבת, then his travel tells us nothing about whether flying above ten טפחים is allowed. The question is still unresolved, and the next step begins another proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe. Often used to reject a proof by offering another possibility.
The demon יוסף, known in the גמרא for passing teachings between the sages

phrases.english: No, perhaps Yosef the demon said them.
phrases.notes: He does not keep שבת, so his travel proves nothing

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the proof from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely, without deciding the question itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the messenger was אליהו, who keeps שבת. But it could have been יוסף שידא, who does not, so his travel shows nothing about the הלכה.

steps.title: A new proof begins: a vow to be a נזיר on the day משיח comes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new proof from a ברייתא. Someone who vows to be a נזיר on the day בן דוד comes may still drink wine on שבתות and ימים טובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone says, 'I am a נזיר on the day that בן דוד comes,' he is allowed to drink wine on שבתות and ימים טובים...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof by quoting the start of a ברייתא. The point of the proof only becomes clear on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person's נזירות starts only when משיח arrives. Since he may drink wine on שבת and יום טוב, the ברייתא assumes משיח (and אליהו, who comes first to announce him) will not arrive on those days. The גמרא will soon ask what this teaches about תחומין above ten טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Behold, I am a נזיר. The words used to take on נזירות.
The son of David, meaning משיח

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished yet. Don't try to pull out the proof about תחומין from these words alone. The גמרא will finish the ברייתא and explain the connection on the next amud.

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'Behold, I am a nazirite'
'on the day that the son of David comes'
phrases.notes: His נזירות begins only when משיח arrives

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר לִשְׁתּוֹת יַיִן בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וּבְיָמִים טוֹבִים,
phrases.english: he is permitted to drink wine on Shabbatot and Festivals,
phrases.notes: Because משיח is assumed not to come on those days

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר בַּיּוֹם שֶׁבֶּן דָּוִד בָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the seven teachings was rejected, the גמרא begins yet another proof, this time from a ברייתא about נזירות.
steps.raayaObject: Whether תחומין apply above ten טפחים (the full argument continues on the next amud)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a vow of נזירות starting on the day בן דוד comes still allows wine on שבתות and ימים טובים
